name: Opt-in local reminders
userOutcome: Choose optional dawn, sunset, or sleep reminders, edit each local time, and retain the previous working setting when scheduling fails, without being forced to grant notification permission.
productionDataSource: UNUserNotificationCenter local calendar notification requests and UserDefaults reminder preferences.
errorBehavior: Onboarding never requests notification permission. Reminder toggles and enabled reminder times update persisted preferences only after UNUserNotificationCenter confirms scheduling; a failed time edit restores the previous displayed and persisted time, leaves the prior stable-ID request in effect, and explains recovery. Foreground reconciliation removes stale enabled toggles when no matching system request remains, and denial offers an Open iOS Settings recovery action.
layoutScenarios: failed time edit restored to previous value
accessibilityRequirements: Each reminder is a labeled system Toggle.
Each enabled reminder has a labeled locale-aware time DatePicker.
Denial and scheduling failure messages are readable by VoiceOver.
No permission request occurs before an explicit opt-in.
prohibitedBehavior: Do not request notification permission on launch.
Do not show a reminder as enabled before scheduling succeeds.
Do not create duplicate requests for repeated taps.
Do not change a reminder's stable notification identifier when its time changes.
Do not persist or continue displaying a new enabled-reminder time before rescheduling succeeds.
Do not treat permission denial as a fatal error.
acceptanceTests: Manual Me-tab opt-in permission grant and denial checks
AppSettingsTests reminder-time persistence and invalid-value recovery
Manual edit, relaunch, failed-update rollback, timezone, and daylight-saving checks
Manual reminder delivery check on a real device
